It is often claimed that a positive outlook is the gateway to success. I agree with this idea in many ways, but I also believe it may not apply to every situation. On one hand, numerous famous individuals have shown that being optimistic helped them achieve their goals. For instance, Michael Jordan was once cut from his high school basketball team, yet his determination and belief in himself drove him to work harder, eventually making him one of the greatest players in history.

Another example comes from the music world. The rapper DaBaby was told for years that he would never make it. Despite this, he remained humble, kept a positive mindset, and continued to pursue his dream. Today he holds multiple gold and platinum albums and has built a massive fan base, demonstrating how a hopeful attitude can lead to real success.

On the other hand, a positive attitude is not always the best approach. In dangerous situations such as combat, soldiers often need to stay alert, realistic, and prepared for threats rather than hopeful. In such cases, optimism alone might not protect them or guarantee victory. In conclusion, maintaining a positive attitude can often be the key to success, but depending on the situation, a more cautious or realistic mindset may be equally important.

Ralph Waldo Emerson wrote, “Unless you try to do something beyond what you have already mastered, you will never grow.” It may work for Ralph Waldo Emerson or other people, but I disagree with what he says. People are different; they have many different ways to make them grow up, not the only way like Ralph Waldo Emerson wrote. People can study new things to make their knowledge more. They can learn from the small mistakes they made. They can grow up from society. In China there are so many reasons that make you grow up.

In China, people do not always follow Ralph Waldo Emerson’s idea that we must attempt things beyond what we already know to grow. I believe everyone is different, so not all of us become more mature simply by moving past our current skills. If someone leaves behind an activity they excel in, it does not mean they have grown. I disagree with Emerson’s claim for three reasons: learning something completely new can lead to growth, small details can prompt personal development, and life events also help us mature.  

First, exploring unfamiliar areas can boost our growth as much as challenging ourselves within our comfort zone. For example, my mother came to the United States without knowing any English. She studied the language for three years and finally reached the point where she could speak basic sentences. No one would say she did not grow just because she chose to learn a language she knew nothing about before. Through her experience, I learned that discovering entirely new subjects can help a person develop, not only stretching one’s current abilities.  

Second, minor mistakes or overlooked details can also teach us important lessons. In a science lab, even a tiny error can ruin an experiment. A student who experiences that failure often learns more about precision and care than someone who only handles simple tasks successfully. Those small chances to notice and correct mistakes push a person to improve their focus and patience. Such moments of learning from the little things are just as valuable for growth.  

Third, real-world experiences like entering the workforce, getting married, or becoming a parent bring new responsibilities that shape our character. School life is very different from professional life. At work, effort alone is not always enough; you must learn various strategies to reach higher levels. When someone gets married, they discover teamwork and compromise. Having a child teaches responsibility in a way that few other things can. These major life changes make a person truly grow into adulthood.  

Emerson wrote, “Unless you try to do something beyond what you have already mastered, you will never grow.” This might hold true for some individuals, but I disagree with his general rule. People can mature by learning brand-new skills, by paying attention to small mistakes, and by facing life’s challenges. In China, many different paths lead to personal growth, not just the one Emerson described.

Sometimes Ralph Waldo Emerson remarks about how facing life can be tough, especially for teenagers. As a child, your future seems more predictable because your family shapes your daily life.

Success often comes from staying active and pursuing our goals without pause. When we take on more tasks, we move closer to the achievements we envision. Consider Thomas Jefferson: in drafting the Declaration of Independence, he dedicated himself fully and did not idle away his time with friends. His example shows that progress depends on constant effort rather than relaxation.

At the start of each year, we choose personal objectives—whether improving grades, learning a language, or saving money. By checking these targets regularly, we remain busy and focused. In contrast, many people lose sight of their aims, allowing distractions to derail their plans. Yet deep down, everyone carries a desire to push forward, finding motivation in their dreams and ambitions.

We see this spirit in every new invention: the latest smartphone, an innovative television, or stylish footwear. Behind each item is a person or team who worked tirelessly to refine ideas and bring them to life. Generations build on past discoveries, continually enhancing our world. This momentum depends on individuals who keep moving, experimenting, and improving year after year.

Education follows the same pattern. Students go to school, advance to college, and then enter the workforce—each stage requiring active participation. By engaging with lessons, internships, or part-time jobs, we gain knowledge and experience that shape our future careers. Every step we take leads us closer to our broader life goals.

Even at home, staying productive matters. During summer break, for instance, some young people might spend hours playing video games and snacking, ignoring chores. When parents see a sink full of dishes or an empty schedule, they often encourage their children to help around the house or find part-time work. These small tasks teach responsibility and show how constant action contributes to personal growth.

In the end, achievement is the result of continuous effort. Each day offers chances to learn, create, and advance. By always doing something—even in small ways—we accumulate successes without even realizing it. Continuous activity truly leads to accomplishment.

“Success is going from failure to failure without losing enthusiasm.” I believe these words from Winston Churchill remind us that persistence matters most. When you truly care about something, you must keep trying even if you stumble along the way. In my own life, I have often begun projects and wondered whether I could finish them. Yet I always return to them because giving up is not an option. Many people start with energy but, after a few setbacks, they quit. To achieve your goals, you must keep chasing them, no matter how hard it seems.

Failure is a strong word that everyone dislikes. For example, when students fail a test, they may feel embarrassed and discouraged. But I have learned that mistakes are part of learning. When I did poorly on my English exam, I reviewed my errors and studied harder. As a result, I improved in the next test. In the workplace, arriving late can block your chances of promotion and higher pay. Being punctual and diligent every day is essential to move forward. In soccer, success comes only through constant practice and correct technique. You must train regularly, learn from each match, and always aim to do better. Even though failure often feels like a waste of time, it teaches resilience and pushes you closer to your dreams.

Enthusiasm is the fuel that powers your journey. Without it, you may stop before reaching your destination. Suppose you start college, then take a job to earn money, and later consider returning to your studies. You might lose the excitement that first drove you, and you could decide not to continue. That lost enthusiasm is what often causes people to quit. If you keep a positive mindset and remind yourself why you began, you can surpass any obstacle.

I agree wholeheartedly with Churchill’s message: to succeed, you must fight for your dreams and never give in to failure. You will stumble, but get up and keep moving forward with energy and confidence. Everyone deserves success, and enthusiasm is the key to achieving it.

Aesop once said, “No act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted.” To me, this means that even when we feel angry or sad, a small gesture can still bring hope or comfort. For instance, losing a family member is painful, but remembering their happier moments can remind us that they are free from suffering.

I also think Aesop wants us to stand up for ourselves and not let others hold us back. If someone tells you that you’re wrong, show them what you can do. You might make mistakes along the way, but each error teaches a lesson and brings you closer to success.

Finally, this quote encourages us to enjoy life’s simple pleasures. As children, we spend our days playing and laughing without worries. As adults, we face responsibilities like jobs, bills, and chores, which leave little time for fun. That’s why it’s important to cherish those small moments of joy while we can.

I believe that collaborating in a group is the most effective way for students to learn. Working together allows everyone to share their thoughts and learn from each other’s viewpoints. For instance, I enjoy hearing different opinions because they often spark fresh ideas about how to approach an assignment. When students have the chance to voice their suggestions, they gain confidence and are more willing to participate without fear of judgment.

Of course, some students prefer to work alone to avoid interruptions or too many questions. They usually arrive at a topic with a clear plan and can maintain their own pace. Studying independently helps them finish tasks on time because they don’t need to coordinate with others or explain their ideas repeatedly.

However, group work also brings the advantage of dividing a project into manageable parts. One person might handle the research, another could focus on design, and someone else might write the report. By choosing the section they feel most comfortable with, students can complete their portion more efficiently and produce higher-quality results.

Another benefit is meeting new classmates. Often, teachers assign groups randomly, so you end up working with people you’ve never met. This exposes you to different techniques—one student might use a T-chart to list pros and cons before deciding which side to argue. Observing such methods can help you discover new ways to organize and present your ideas.

Moreover, projects move faster when tasks are shared. If you finish your assignment early, you can assist teammates who may be struggling. For example, a student working alone might take longer to complete a section, but you can offer your help and ensure the entire group stays on schedule.

In conclusion, group work teaches students to respect and build on each other’s perspectives, making it an excellent way to achieve a common goal. Still, some argue that working independently fosters decision-making skills and self-reliance, showing that both approaches have valuable lessons to offer.

People often face the question: should they rely on their own choices or follow the advice of experts and authorities? I believe that making our own decisions is more valuable because it leads to personal learning from mistakes, allows us to create rules that fit our needs, and prevents others from controlling our path.

First of all, when we decide for ourselves, we gain real experience by dealing with the outcomes of our actions. If a choice ends badly, it becomes a lesson. For example, someone who starts a small project alone might lose money at first, but they learn how to manage resources and plan more carefully next time. Moreover, encountering challenges alone forces us to find creative solutions. This direct feedback helps us develop problem-solving skills that no lecture or book can provide. Over time, we become more responsible, confident, and better at making future decisions. Such growth also shows others that we can overcome difficulties without outside direction, and it inspires further trust and respect.

Another benefit of independence is that we can set our own guidelines. By creating rules that match our values and goals, we know why each rule exists and what to expect from it. For instance, by arranging our own study schedule, we can choose hours when we feel most focused instead of following someone else’s timetable. If we launch a side business based on our hobby, we can decide how much time and money to invest without waiting for approval. In contrast, obeying another person’s rules can be confusing if their reasons are unclear or their methods do not suit us. When we control our own planning, we gain clarity, stay organized, and increase our satisfaction and success rate.

Finally, making decisions alone keeps others from interfering unnecessarily. If we rely on more experienced people, they might correct every step or impose their methods on us. In a workplace, an independent employee can test new ideas immediately instead of seeking constant permission. Without constant monitoring, we maintain our motivation. Being free to choose our direction boosts our passion and drive. This autonomy encourages innovation and helps us become leaders in our field. People notice our self-reliance and view us as role models, not just followers.

In conclusion, choosing to act independently rather than simply following experts brings many advantages. We learn much more from our own mistakes, enjoy the freedom of self-made rules, and avoid unwanted interference. Although seeking advice can sometimes be useful, true growth often comes when we trust our own judgment, start from scratch, and build our unique path on the basis of personal experience and responsibility.

First impressions often define how others perceive us and can be very hard to alter. The very first image we present becomes a reference point in people’s minds, influencing their judgments and the way they interact with us. Because this initial encounter feels so authentic, most people stick to it rather than rethink their assumptions.

When someone forms a negative opinion at first, that view tends to persist. Even if our mood or circumstances caused an unfriendly reaction, others may hold on to the idea that we are naturally rude or distant. They remember what happened in that early meeting and use it as evidence to confirm their beliefs about us every time they see us again.

Trying to correct a poor first impression is challenging because people often doubt sudden changes in behavior. If we later make an effort to be polite or warm, others might suspect we are being insincere or hiding our true selves. Their initial judgment creates a filter through which they evaluate all our later actions.

Moreover, we tend to be treated according to how we treated others at the start. If we were courteous, we usually receive kindness in return; if we were abrupt, we might face coldness. This cycle reinforces the original opinion and makes it more difficult for either side to break free from the pattern.

Although first impressions carry a lot of weight, it is possible to change them with consistent effort and genuine intentions. By showing dependable kindness, honesty, and patience over time, we can gradually reshape someone’s perspective. Actions speak louder than words, so steady, positive behavior can replace an unfair first judgment with a more accurate and lasting understanding.

Working with others offers clear advantages compared to working by yourself. When you join a group, you can exchange ideas, support each other, and feel less stressed. In contrast, working alone means relying entirely on your own thoughts, with no one to turn to when you get stuck. Here are three reasons why I prefer group work over working individually.

First, collaborating makes tasks easier and faster to finish. In a team, everyone contributes their knowledge and skills, so we can divide the work and meet deadlines more comfortably. Sharing information also helps us learn from one another. When each member brings their insights, the entire group benefits and stays motivated to reach our goal.

Second, group work provides stronger support than working alone. If someone doesn’t understand a problem, a teammate can explain it or suggest alternative approaches. This back-and-forth helps us overcome challenges and boosts our confidence. In contrast, when you work solo and hit a roadblock, there is no one to ask for help. You have to figure everything out by yourself, which can be difficult and time-consuming.

Third, working in a group reduces stress and frustration. When you know others are there to help, you feel more relaxed. Mistakes become learning opportunities because teammates can offer constructive feedback. On the other hand, working alone can lead to anxiety, since there is no one to review your ideas. If your solution is not good, you might feel disappointed and struggle to improve.

By contrast, working alone forces you to fully support your own ideas, leaves you without help when you’re confused, and often leads to greater frustration. For these reasons—sharing workload, receiving support, and lowering stress—I find group work far more effective and enjoyable than working by myself.

Some people believe that success means moving from one failure to another without ever losing enthusiasm. I agree with this view because every person faces setbacks on the way to their goals. Even those who seem to succeed at everything have usually learned from mistakes and kept their spirits high.

If someone becomes tired or discouraged, friends and family should offer support. A few encouraging words or a helping hand can remind them that they still have the energy and ability to try again. This kind of help shows them that setbacks do not define their future.

No matter how difficult a situation seems, we can resist giving up and find solutions to our problems. Every obstacle can be overcome if we remain determined and hopeful. Some argue that success is almost impossible without enthusiasm, so it is wise to prepare for challenges and keep our motivation strong.

In this way, we can build a happier, more successful life by facing each failure with fresh energy and confidence.

One time my friend used different kinds of drugs—cocaine, marijuana, cigarettes, alcohol, and so on. One day he asked me which school I was attending. When I told him “Generic School,” he asked if he could go with me. I agreed immediately. He explained he was tired of his drug life and wanted to become someone new. From that moment on, he turned his life around. Now he hopes to study medicine and help others transform their lives too. I completely agree with Emerson’s idea of individuality because it shows that real change comes from action, not just words. Taking control of my own life has been my greatest achievement.

I believe in being myself regardless of others’ opinions. If I decide to become a teacher, I must follow my own path, even if people say teaching isn’t important or well paid. They might argue teachers earn only $1,000 a month, but if I love teaching, salary doesn’t matter. Negative people often try to make us doubt ourselves because they gave up on their own dreams. Yet the world is always changing, and I want to prove them wrong. That’s why I ignore anyone who tries to confuse me.

There is a big difference between talking and doing. I could boast about great plans, but without action, my words are empty. I prefer to show my change through my behavior rather than just speak about it. When people notice my efforts, they ask what happened, and I tell them I chose a new direction. That achievement means more than any promise.

Even with self-belief, I must stay focused. As humans, we make mistakes, and some will try to distract me from my goals. For example, many say studying is boring and want me to waste my time. I must resist and remember my dream of becoming someone valuable in the world.

In conclusion, true individuality is not easy. We don’t always need others’ approval—just confidence in ourselves. We must ignore negative comments, act instead of just talking, and stay focused on our goals. Becoming a better person is the greatest achievement. The world needs me.

People often seek advice when they face a challenge or feel confused. Gathering different viewpoints helps in three important ways: it stops bad decisions, checks which advice is reliable, and boosts confidence in the choice. By asking several people, we can usually reach a better decision.

First, getting multiple opinions can prevent us from making mistakes. For example, if you think about taking something that does not belong to you or spending too much on an expensive item, friends or family might warn you against it. When you are involved in an argument or considering dishonest behavior, others can advise you to act more wisely. Hearing different sides often helps avoid actions you would later regret.

Second, comparing several opinions makes it easier to tell which advice is accurate. If most people give the same suggestion but a few disagree, you can trust the majority view more. When you doubt a comment, you can ask someone else to see if it matches their experience. This method helps you find advice that is backed by more evidence or expertise.

Third, seeking various viewpoints gives you greater security in your decision. When you feel lost or worried, talking to others can reassure you that your choice is sound. Advice from friends can also provide emotional support and reduce loneliness. Knowing that you have considered different opinions makes you feel more certain about your actions.

In summary, listening to several opinions prevents poor choices, confirms reliable advice, and increases confidence. Although thinking for ourselves is important, consulting others often leads to smarter and more secure decisions. While personal reflection has its place, I believe gathering multiple opinions is even more crucial for making well-informed choices.

There should be a dedicated after-school homework club at my school to help students improve their grades. Many pupils struggle to complete assignments correctly and need extra guidance. By staying after class, teachers can assist those who feel confused about the day’s material. This one-on-one or small-group help would boost students’ understanding before tests, so they can earn better marks instead of falling behind.

Unfortunately, some students refuse to attend these sessions. Teachers volunteer their free time to stay after school, but too often those who signed up simply do not show. This wastes the teachers’ efforts and leaves other pupils without support. As a result, some teachers stop offering extra time because they feel students do not respect their commitment. If everyone knew there was only one reliable homework club, more pupils might take it seriously and arrive ready to work.

Sometimes classmates who finish early could help but end up chatting or playing games instead of tutoring. When peer-helpers do attempt to assist, they often just give out answers without explaining their thinking. Later, if a teacher asks how they arrived at a solution, neither student can explain, revealing that copying is not effective learning. A structured homework club with teacher oversight would ensure that helpers guide others properly and encourage genuine understanding.

In addition to teacher support, incentives could motivate attendance. For example, pupils who regularly stay for the homework club and complete their work on time might earn recognition, such as certificates or small rewards. Knowing their efforts will be acknowledged could inspire more students to take part. Moreover, keeping parents informed about their child’s progress encourages responsibility. If a student misses club sessions repeatedly, teachers could contact their parents so everyone works together to improve the situation.

Some students prefer finishing homework during free time in class to avoid staying late. The homework club could accommodate these learners by offering a quiet space during study periods, where they can get help without fully extending the school day. Others enjoy collaborative learning, so pairing them with classmates who have the same assignment can help them ask questions and learn from each other, as long as a teacher monitors the session to keep discussions on track.

Overall, a single, well-organized after-school homework club would help more students complete assignments, understand lessons better, and perform well on tests. It would save teachers from spreading their efforts too thin across different classes, ensure peer helpers offer real guidance, and encourage students to be responsible for their own learning. By offering clear support and positive incentives, the school can raise achievement and help every pupil succeed.

Imagine a world where every student stays home and attends classes online. For those who are too ill to go to school—perhaps people battling cancer or recovering in the hospital—online lessons can be a real lifeline. They allow students to keep up with their studies without risking their health. Still, many believe that unless you are genuinely unwell, you should come to school in person. After all, classrooms offer more than just academic instruction; they provide opportunities for sports, socializing, and forming friendships that virtual lessons cannot fully replicate.

I remember when I was five years old, I caught a terrible cold and refused to go to school. I cried so much that my grandfather stepped in. He told me stories of his own childhood when there were no online classes. Despite facing serious difficulties, he attended every lesson and later became a doctor. His determination showed me that physical presence in school can teach resilience and discipline in ways that screens cannot.

Now that I am eighteen, I appreciate my grandfather’s wisdom more than ever. I understand that while online classes are valuable for those who cannot leave home, they cannot replace the experience of being in a classroom. True education requires effort, interaction, and sometimes a bit of discomfort. In the end, whether we choose online or traditional schooling, our choices shape our future path—toward a bright life, making our families proud, and pursuing higher education together.

With this approach, teachers have a set time to organize games, workshops, or creative projects that keep students interested and motivated. After classes finish early, pupils can return home feeling refreshed, catch up on any unfinished assignments, and study at their own pace. Although some critics worry that sending children home sooner might disrupt routines or create too much free time, I believe that varying the daily schedule prevents boredom and helps students stay focused. Furthermore, a shorter school day gives staff extra hours to prepare lessons and improve resources for the following day. Overall, a well-structured half-day plan can boost learning, encourage productivity, and bring a new energy to the school environment.

Has technology affected our lives more negatively than positively? In my view, it has harmed us because people no longer control how much they use it. Nowadays, we forget how wonderful life can be without screens. There are plenty of activities we can enjoy offline, such as playing outdoors with friends, visiting libraries, or simply spending time in nature. While some believe teenagers should have unlimited access to computers and phones to learn more, I feel they need clear boundaries. Parents must also check what their children do online.

Although it’s true that unrestricted internet use can help young people gain valuable skills for the future, it also prevents them from completing tasks through real human contact. Talking face to face not only builds stronger relationships but also teaches social skills. Meeting strangers online is risky since not everyone has good intentions. Many parents assume their children are only playing safe games, but in reality, kids may be exposed to harmful content. Until you really know someone, your conversations and gaming time should be limited.

Another serious issue is online shopping. People often buy many items without verifying who is selling them, which can be dangerous. Some websites genuinely offer the products they advertise, but others exist only to steal money. If you plan to buy something online, always ensure the site is secure. Overreliance on e-commerce also means people spend less time with family, preferring the convenience of sites like Amazon or eBay. Scammers create fake shops to take advantage of unsuspecting customers.

To encourage children to spend less time on technology, parents can organize fun outdoor activities or playgroup gatherings. Forming friendships through video games or social media is not healthy for kids until they have met those friends in person. Some strangers may even persuade children to do unsafe things.

For all these reasons, I believe technology should either be restricted for children or used under strict parental supervision. Without setting limits, people lose real-life skills, become targets for fraud, and risk missing out on a true childhood.

Many schools now offer distance learning so that students can join classes online from home. However, this approach often does more harm than good. At home, students face numerous distractions such as televisions, video games, and mobile phones. While a few may find self-study easier, most struggle to concentrate and end up browsing the internet for answers or even copying assignments from online sources.

Another problem is the lack of social interaction. In a classroom, students work together on projects, share ideas, and build friendships. By studying alone at home, they miss out on these group activities, and their motivation can drop. Some argue that learning from home reduces bullying based on skin color or appearance, but the benefit is small compared to the loss of teamwork and peer support.

Daily routines also suffer with distance learning. When students study from home, they may skip morning routines like showering or wake up late, which affects their productivity. In contrast, going to school creates a structured day, with regular breaks, lunch time, and access to the library where they can find textbooks and notebooks for homework.

Cost is another important factor. Video conferences and specialized online platforms often require extra fees. Many students already hold part-time jobs to pay for tuition, and these additional expenses can be a heavy burden. In a physical school, most educational materials and facilities are included, so families do not face unexpected charges.

Finally, direct contact with teachers makes learning easier. In class, a student can immediately ask for clarification, get help with difficult tasks, and receive detailed feedback. Online, communication is slower and less personal, so misunderstandings remain unresolved longer.

For these reasons, attending classes at home via video conferencing is not a good idea for most students. The distractions, extra costs, and lack of face-to-face support outweigh any benefits.

Businesses can save energy and resources by moving to a four-day workweek with longer days. Resources such as land, minerals or natural energy are limited, so reducing the days we operate could cut down on costs and environmental impact. Although some people worry this change might hurt productivity, many large companies have found that a shorter week helps them in the long term. They not only gain in efficiency but also build a reputation for caring about sustainability and employee well-being.

Schools could also try a similar model, but with smaller changes. For example, classes might run two extra hours on certain days instead of adding a full extra day. Not everyone would need to join, but those who do could help lower the school’s overall use of electricity, heating and other resources. This approach would teach students about conservation while still covering the required material.

The key to success is finding the right balance of hours so that work or study remains effective. If we plan carefully, a shorter week can save energy and resources, benefit the environment and still keep productivity high.

I believe that, together, we can build a government that truly serves all Americans.

People often find themselves in good moods when something pleasant happens, and they usually prefer to stay happy rather than dwell on negative feelings. Sometimes we seek out fun activities simply to lift our spirits and forget about what’s bothering us. Ideally, everyone would feel cheerful all the time and avoid sadness, anger, or frustration.

However, bad moods do occur for many reasons. You might wake up feeling grumpy, or your parents could be upset with you over something you didn’t do. When people face unfair criticism or have a rough start to the day, it’s easy to remain unhappy. Despite this, most people do try to maintain a positive attitude and wonder why small issues can trigger so much anger.

It’s important to support others when they’re down. If you see someone getting bullied or struggling with their emotions, reach out and offer kindness. Be friendly, listen to them, and encourage them to talk with someone they trust, like a teacher or a close friend. Avoid getting too close to people who put you down or act like they don’t care about your feelings. Instead, surround yourself with honest friends who lift you up.

Believe in yourself and never give up. If someone says you can’t achieve something, don’t let their words hold you back. Always do your best, whether at school or in your personal life. Life is too short to stay in a bad mood—choose to be kind, stay positive, and build genuine relationships that help everyone feel happier.

People often ask why making our own choices matters. I believe we all need to decide for ourselves because it brings freedom, clarity, and satisfaction. When we choose our own path, we understand our reasons and feel more confident in our lives.

Firstly, deciding on our own gives us more independence. If we let others choose for us, we might feel restricted or unhappy. But when we pick what suits us best—studies, work, or hobbies—we take control of our future and accept responsibility for our actions.

Secondly, making personal choices helps us know what we truly want. Reflecting on our goals and preferences reduces confusion and doubt. Understanding why we make a particular decision also prepares us to face any outcomes, turning challenges into opportunities to learn.

Additionally, living by our own decisions can make life simpler. If someone else decides for us, their ideas might not match our values or tastes, leading to frustration. By choosing for ourselves, we align our actions with what we enjoy and believe in, so everyday tasks and long-term plans feel natural and manageable.

There is also the risk of conflict when our choices clash with those of others. If two people have different ideas, forcing one view on another creates tension. When each person has the freedom to decide, we respect individual rights and avoid unnecessary disputes.

In conclusion, making our own decisions is essential for independence, clarity, and peace of mind. It helps us learn, grow, and lead a life that reflects our true selves. Therefore, everyone should have the chance and the responsibility to choose their own way.

Nowadays, technology has become an essential part of our everyday lives, and I believe its impact is mostly positive. As new devices and applications appear, they make many tasks easier and open up fresh opportunities. Whether it’s staying in touch with friends or finding information quickly, modern tools help us navigate daily routines more smoothly than ever before.

One clear benefit is how technology improves communication and convenience. For example, video calls and messaging apps let us talk to people around the world instantly. Online shopping saves time, too, since you can buy groceries or clothes without leaving home. Digital maps and GPS services guide us to new places, removing the need for paper maps. Even banking has moved online, so you can deposit checks or transfer money with just a few clicks. And when you want to relax, playing video games or streaming music is always an option.

However, it’s important to know how to use these tools properly. If someone lacks basic computer skills or isn’t familiar with certain apps, they may feel frustrated when trying to complete simple tasks. That’s why practice and learning are essential. You can follow tutorials, attend courses, or ask friends for guidance. When you understand how a device or program works, you are less likely to make mistakes and more able to use technology for good rather than harmful purposes.

At the same time, we should be aware of potential downsides, especially for children. Young people who spend too much time on screens may neglect schoolwork, physical activity, or face-to-face interaction. Setting clear limits on how long and when they use devices can help maintain a healthy balance. Parents and teachers should guide them and encourage other interests, such as sports or reading, so technology doesn’t become the only focus in their lives.

In conclusion, technology offers us incredible advantages, from connecting with friends to managing our finances online. Yet it also demands responsibility: we must learn how to use it well, set sensible boundaries, and think before acting. By seeking advice when we need it and reflecting on our choices, we can enjoy all the positive aspects of technology without letting it control us.

When you face a challenge you have already attempted and it ends in failure, it’s easy to feel discouraged. However, each effort you make can help you develop greater strength and self-control. Stay calm, believe in your potential, and trust that new possibilities will open. Exploring fresh activities shows you how much you can achieve. Ultimately, success depends on your commitment: if you truly want something, go for it. Don’t be swayed by other people’s doubts – no one else determines your life.

The idea that repeating a failed task proves you will never improve is mistaken. A setback does not signal the end of your growth. Quite the opposite: when you are determined to pursue a goal, you must be prepared to face defeat several times before achieving progress. Persistence means not becoming weary until you reach your dream.

My father’s experience as a singer illustrates this. He joined a major music project and was well prepared, but on the day of the performance he completely lost his voice. Still, he gave his all and impressed the judges. After that, many people contacted him for new collaborations. Today, he is a star who continues to develop his talent. His story shows that by believing in yourself and refusing to give up, you can advance remarkably.

I have faced similar struggles. When I arrived in the United States, I did not speak any English. Every assignment felt challenging and I often worried I would fail. Yet I kept pushing forward, studying hard and trying new methods. Over time, my language skills improved and I grew in confidence. I am still learning and discovering new abilities through perseverance.

Some argue that spending too much time perfecting one skill is a waste of life, while others believe mastery guarantees a bright future. In reality, those who keep trying, despite risks and failures, are the ones who achieve their goals. Never stop believing in yourself, ignore negative comments, and continue working toward what you want. Everything depends on your own efforts.

Although some people believe that students’ self-esteem should come from praise—especially when they are preparing for exams or trying to pass a course—I think genuine confidence is built through real accomplishments. In conclusion, while praise can feel encouraging in the short term, true self-esteem grows from the effort, energy, and ongoing work that students put into their academic goals. By achieving genuine results, they develop lasting confidence in their own skills.

On the other hand, working solo can be tough. When you face several tasks by yourself, it’s hard to know if you will finish on time, especially if they are large. A big project might take you a whole day or more to complete alone.

I have experienced both situations. Once, my team was asked to prepare six pallets and we had only two left to finish. We coordinated well and completed the work so quickly that we expected to leave early, but we stayed until the job was done.

By contrast, doing the same task alone was very challenging because the pallet had so much stuff that I couldn’t even finish one. Since I was new in that department, they eventually sent someone to help me.

Overall, teamwork offers more benefits than working alone, except for small tasks that one person can easily handle.

I agree that the three words—anxiety, expressing feelings, and self-belief—capture important parts of our emotional lives.

First, anxiety touches many of us. A large number of people worry constantly about tasks, decisions, or personal problems. That mental pressure can feel overwhelming when it stays inside. If we never share our fears, we miss chances to find solutions or support. Holding onto anxiety makes it hard to change our situation and move on.

Second, expressing feelings is essential. Some people keep their emotions hidden because they don’t know how to explain what they truly want or need. This uncertainty breeds silence and fear of judgment, so they choose not to speak up. Yet without honest communication, misunderstandings grow and opportunities for connection slip away.

Third, believing in oneself supports every action we take. At times, individuals lack confidence and ask others to complete tasks they feel ashamed to tackle on their own. This dependence can deepen self-doubt and block personal growth. By trusting our abilities and taking responsibility, we learn new skills and build genuine respect for ourselves.

Life may present many challenges, but it is not impossible. Over time, everything changes—our friends, our circumstances, even our feelings. We should not feel ashamed to ask for what we need or to say what we want. Mistakes are part of learning and guide us toward improvement. If we choose positive paths and have faith in ourselves, we can live fully without being overwhelmed by anxiety or self-doubt.

I believe that being yourself is essential for developing into a good person. If we don’t act authentically, we miss the chance to build a genuine character and earn true respect.

First, authenticity helps build a strong personality. When you behave naturally, you gain confidence and the appreciation of others. In contrast, pretending to be someone else prevents you from forming honest relationships and positive traits.

Second, self-confidence is closely tied to kindness and respect. People who trust their own values are more likely to treat others well. By showing honesty and generosity, we create a supportive community and inspire those around us.

Furthermore, staying true to ourselves helps us avoid constant comparison and unnecessary competition. When you accept your unique qualities, you focus on personal growth instead of measuring success against others. This leads to a more peaceful and respectful attitude.

In conclusion, being yourself nurtures confidence, respect, and generosity. These qualities not only improve our own lives but also benefit the people around us. Therefore, staying authentic is the key to becoming a truly good person.

Consider a scenario where classes run two hours beyond the current schedule every day. This change would leave pupils without any spare time once lessons finish, preventing them from pursuing their interests or relaxing. As a result, learners might grow weary and develop a dislike for school.

By adding extra hours, students would find it impossible to take part in sports teams or participate in clubs. They would have no chance to practise their favourite activities or meet friends in these settings. Opportunities for creative projects, music lessons or community events after class would vanish, which could harm their physical and emotional well-being.

Furthermore, extended days would sap pupils’ energy. Arriving home tired, they might struggle to concentrate on homework or enjoy quality moments with family. Some could even skip school occasionally just to escape the additional hours, causing irregular attendance and a lack of motivation. Over time, the stress and fatigue could undermine their performance and enthusiasm for learning.

In conclusion, prolonging the school day by two hours would disrupt young people’s routines, reduce free time for activities and strain their energy levels. To help students lead balanced lives and stay engaged with their studies, it is best to maintain the current timetable.

With more time, they can explore different subjects, join clubs, play games, and prepare thoroughly for exams. Many also value the chance to spend extra time with friends and learn from teachers they admire. For these reasons, the usual four-year path remains popular for high school students.

Engaging in enjoyable educational activities offers a valuable way to learn while having fun. These activities can be carried out wherever and whenever we choose, giving learners the freedom to fit study into their own schedules. Thomas Jefferson’s words remind us that people should never remain idle but should strive to achieve great things together and find meaning in life. I believe Jefferson meant that if the colonies united and decided whether to remain under strict British rule or fight for freedom, they could accomplish remarkable goals. We shed our blood alongside the British in the French and Indian War, yet when it ended, King George took control of new lands and prevented colonists from settling there. Meanwhile, we were forced to pay taxes to a monarch who cared only about his wealth and authority.

If we did not resist, our lives would resemble those of slaves. We would have no voice, watching our families go hungry under arbitrary taxes. The British labelled us traitors and threatened to kill us, but what of the mothers and children left behind to suffer? If we choose to die for liberty, we die as free people, not as subjects.

Jefferson’s writings in newspapers and pamphlets opened American eyes to the truth: we no longer had to obey a distant king. As Americans, we could govern ourselves and elect our own leaders. No single individual can manage every matter across the ocean, but if we stand together, we can achieve anything. In unity and determination, we secure our freedom and shape our own destiny.

In my view, offering classes online or via video chat is an excellent idea for students, especially those who live far from school. This approach gives learners the chance to study when travel is impractical. For instance, during snowstorms schools often close because roads become dangerous and buses cannot run. In such cases, virtual lessons keep students on track without risking their safety.

Another advantage is ease and speed. Online learning tools are usually simple to use, so students can attend lessons from home without wasting time on the commute. This flexibility also creates more free time, allowing learners to take on part-time work or pursue other interests while studying.

However, remote classes have downsides. Some students lack computers or reliable internet access, making it hard for them to participate. Although online lessons are a great choice for many, they are not suitable for everyone due to these technical barriers.

To ensure fairness, I believe free online schools should be available to all students at no cost. Additionally, virtual classes should offer flexible schedules so learners can start lessons at convenient times and never miss important content. Overall, I think that remote learning is an effective and modern way to educate students.

Former British prime minister Winston Churchill once said that success is moving from one failure to another without losing enthusiasm. This means that setbacks do not determine our worth; instead, our willingness to try again leads us forward. Although it can be tempting to copy the decisions of those we admire, only we can fully understand how a particular choice will affect our future.

At first, I considered asking people who had already made that move for their opinion. They might have warned me about the challenges or praised the benefits, but in the end I realised that no one else could feel my hopes, fears, or priorities exactly as I did. So I made the choice myself, accepting that it was my responsibility to live with the results.

In those cases, parents or guardians ideally act in our best interests, guided by their experience and care. Every decision carries consequences, and only we can weigh those outcomes against our own dreams and needs.

We cannot erase the impressions we collect in our minds, nor can we change those from our past. I still recall three important moments that shaped my life.

The first one came when I was around six. My parents almost divorced, and their constant arguments filled our home with pain and confusion. At that time, I thought my world would collapse. Although it hurt me deeply, I now see that I learned about the impact of family relationships and the value of harmony.

My second memory is a happier one. My uncle asked me, “Do you want to live in the United States?” Hearing that question filled me with excitement. Since then, I have dreamed of starting a new life abroad and discovering fresh opportunities. This hope encouraged me to study English harder and imagine a different future.

The last impression was the passing of my best friend in Guatemala due to a strange illness. Losing him was the most painful experience I have ever known. His death changed my view of life and reminded me how fragile our time can be.

These three events taught me that while we cannot change past impressions, we can shape the future. Learning from past experiences gives us the strength to move forward and create new, positive memories. By reflecting on these moments, I find motivation to embrace whatever comes next and continue my journey.

Well, hello. Today I will discuss the difference between working with a group or working alone. First, let me ask you a question: How do you like to work? With a group or alone? Well, I chose working with a group. Let’s see why…

Working in a group and working alone have advantages and disadvantages for each one. I like working as a group because your team can help you with some ideas and ways to do your work and at the same time have fun while you are doing the work. Disadvantages in a group: there will always be a person who wants to be just playing around and doesn’t like to do any type of work, just have fun. But if we are on the side of working alone, that advantage will be that you will have more opportunity to do your work the way you want to and not be worried about other people’s opinions. You will finish your work faster and the way you want the work to be done, but some disadvantages are that you will not have fun because you have no one to be with and it will be difficult to have a lot of ideas. I think working with a group is more beneficial because, if you think, there will be more people at the presentation helping you and you will feel more secure with your work.

Working with a group can help you to increase your skill level of talking and self-confidence and being social (meet new friends). Working alone can sometimes get boring and you don’t finish the work because you don’t have someone to share ideas with.

Working alone can cause you damage to your personality and your appearance and people will think if you don’t like working with another person around that you should work by yourself and then there will be a lot of chaos; that person will fall into depression because no one accepts him and it was because you made them feel that way.

While you are working with a group you learn skills like having respect for others and different ways of doing things and work as a team, or even, for example, you love to play sports, well, you cannot do it by yourself because there will be a team, and how will you work as a team without learning how to work as a group, you need to learn how to work as a team if you want to be successful in the community, in your future. Working with a group with the people you trust you learn that friendship is always good for you; you have that confidence that people you like being with help you to increase in your life, that is a feeling that no one can easily afford it.

When you are working with a group friendship will always be there; why? Because it is the key of being successful in your life, in your future, and your career, in your job.

For example: let’s say that you were driving on the highway driving normally, but you forgot to pass by the gas station; you are in the middle of the street and you don’t have gas. Well, if you don’t like to work with a group then you will push your car and probably you will end up getting a disease or crashing another car.

While if you learn how to work as a group then you can have four people helping you push your car, others stopping the traffic and some calling the police to help you with that issue.

Now you see why it is important to learn and work as a group, even though with that you already meet new people and have new friends. What I try to say is that working with a group helps you a lot in harder things that you need help with.

Working alone is dependent on what kind of personality you have and if you love working without people then it’s fine but there will always be a time that you have to work as a team or group because there are things that someone by themselves cannot accomplish.

When you work as a group you gain respect and great friendship because if you help with everything then everyone will love working with you and you will now feel that you are important and useful, something that working alone will be difficult to make.

I did my best and I feel that we should be more socialized with others and let them join us for our better future so they can have friends and never feel like they are alone. Let’s make everyone happy and have a good time helping others and always be respectful.

Have you ever wondered whether you work better alone or as part of a team? I prefer working with a group, and there are several reasons why I think it is more advantageous.

First of all, collaborating with others means you can share ideas and approaches to a task. When you have classmates or colleagues around, everyone can contribute suggestions that you might never have thought of on your own. Group work can also be more enjoyable, because you can chat, encourage each other, and turn a project into a shared experience. Of course, there is a downside: sometimes someone in the group may not take the work seriously and prefers to joke around instead of helping. Even so, I find the positive aspects outweigh this drawback.

On the other hand, working alone gives you complete control over how you complete your tasks. You don’t need to compromise with anyone else’s opinions, so you may finish your work more quickly and exactly as you want. However, this independence can become boring, as there is no one to discuss ideas with or to make the process more lively. You may end up feeling isolated and lacking creative input.

Teamwork does more than just make tasks fun; it also helps improve communication skills and self-confidence. When you speak in front of a group, you learn to express your thoughts clearly and to listen respectfully to others. Meeting new people and forming friendships can boost your social life and help you feel supported. In contrast, spending too much time alone might harm your mood or self-esteem, because people could assume you dislike cooperating, and you could start feeling left out.

Learning to work well with others builds respect and understanding of different approaches. For example, in sports, you cannot play a team game entirely by yourself; you must trust your teammates and coordinate your actions. These experiences teach you to rely on others and to give and receive help. In the future, whether at university or in a job, successful teamwork is often essential, so getting used to it early is a big advantage.

Imagine you are driving on the motorway, and your car runs out of petrol. If you insisted on doing everything alone, you might have to push the car by yourself, which could be exhausting or even dangerous. But if you have friends or colleagues with you, some could help push, others could direct traffic, and someone might call roadside assistance. That cooperation is a clear example of why group effort can solve problems more safely and quickly.

Of course, working solo can suit people who enjoy independence, but eventually most of us will face tasks that require more than one pair of hands. By cooperating with reliable teammates, you gain respect, build lasting friendships, and feel valuable. For these reasons, I believe group work is more beneficial than working alone. Let us be open to others, include everyone, and build a supportive environment so that no one feels left out and everyone enjoys working together.

My first important reason why I disagree with Emerson’s statement about individuality is this: a human being, if he wants to be the greatest accomplishment, cannot achieve it by himself because he needs help from school or a teacher. You can’t do that without help.

My most important reason why I disagree with Emerson’s statement about individuality is this: to be the greatest accomplishment, you need to study what you want to be. I disagree with Ralph Waldo Emerson’s statement that being yourself in a world seeking to change you is the highest achievement. In reality, individual success often relies on help and interaction with others. First, education and mentorship play a vital role: students need teachers and mentors to guide them and provide feedback, without which it is hard to grow. Second, working with peers in groups helps to develop ideas more fully than working alone. Teamwork brings different viewpoints together, making it easier to overcome challenges and discover new approaches. Additionally, becoming truly accomplished requires a solid foundation of knowledge. People must study various subjects, learn about the world, and build on the expertise of others. This continuous learning process shapes a person’s abilities far beyond what pure self-reliance can achieve. In conclusion, while Emerson glorifies self-dependence, real accomplishments stem from collaboration, education, and shared experiences. It is through combining our individual efforts with the support of others that we reach our greatest potential.

Many students wonder whether it’s wise to decide on a career while still young. There are both positive and negative aspects to choosing a profession at an early age.

On the positive side, young people often view the world with fresh eyes. Their creativity and enthusiasm help them imagine paths that older individuals might find impossible. By focusing on a specific goal early, they can tailor their studies, seek relevant experiences, and build useful connections. This focused approach may lead to internships, scholarships, and other opportunities that strengthen their future success.

However, there are drawbacks to making such an important decision too soon. Teenagers usually have limited life experiences and may not fully understand their true interests. Without exposure to a variety of fields, they risk committing to a profession that might not suit them, which can later cause frustration and require a major change in direction.

Consider a seventeenth-grade student who starts working part-time to support a single mother. At first, juggling a job and school feels overwhelming. Yet the student’s determination to help the family and complete an education shows that young people can handle significant responsibilities. This example illustrates that with motivation and planning, even teenagers facing hardship can progress toward their career goals.

In conclusion, choosing a career at a young age has both benefits and challenges. Youthful imagination and energy open doors, but a lack of real-world experience can lead to missteps. Ultimately, with persistence, flexibility, and a willingness to learn, any student—regardless of age—can successfully shape their future.

I believe Thomas Jefferson’s advice is valuable, although opinions on it vary—some agree with him, while others disagree. People often share different views about how to spend their time and whether constant activity is truly beneficial.

I support Jefferson’s message for several reasons. First, by putting effort into our tasks every day, we can achieve more than if we delay our work. Second, Jefferson himself was a respected thinker whose dedication can motivate us not to give up when things become difficult. While a few argue that resting and taking breaks have their own benefits, I feel that staying active and tackling tasks as soon as possible leads to better results. Inactivity rarely brings positive changes or progress.

In summary, I think adopting Jefferson’s attitude—avoiding excuses, keeping busy, and completing tasks promptly—can help us succeed in life.

Ralph Waldo Emerson famously wrote, “To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment.” I completely agree. In a society where so many forces push us to conform, remaining true to our own identity is indeed a significant achievement.

Today, individuals in all fields feel pressure to fit a mold. Take artists, for example—whether they make music, paint, or write—they often strive to bring something new to their craft. A teacher might design a unique lesson plan that no one else has tried before. This innovation can lead to either success or criticism, since people are quick to judge anything that seems different. Yet those very judgments show how the world is always attempting to reshape us; our response to that pressure defines our originality.

Negative attitudes from others can be powerful, but resisting them builds our inner strength. Imagine classmates mocking your style or ideas. You can respond by staying confident and remembering that no one is perfect. Each person has the right to be distinctive, and we can draw inspiration from those who have passed—family members, historical figures, or trailblazing creators. Consider the founder of Facebook: his bold idea changed how billions of people connect, proving that following your own vision can have a wide-reaching positive impact.

Life follows a natural cycle: birth, growth, reproduction, and death. During the growth stage, we face choices that shape our future. Teachers and parents often ask, “What do you want to become when you grow up?” This question highlights our opportunity to contribute something valuable to the world. Teenagers choosing a college major or career should feel free to follow their interests, even if others disapprove.

In the end, outside opinions lose their power when we stay true to ourselves. We each have only one life, and deciding how to live it is our own responsibility. By embracing our individuality, learning from past role models, and brushing off unfair criticism, we can achieve the greatest accomplishment: being ourselves in a world determined to change us.

People often let other people’s judgments shape who they are. It is natural to worry about how friends, family members, or partners see us, especially when we love them and fear upsetting or losing them.

John Lubbock once wrote, “Your character will be what you yourself choose to make of it.” His words really influenced me. Although many might disagree, I believe he is right: our character should not be dictated by others’ opinions or by negative events. We control our thoughts and actions, and we decide what kind of person to become. I have seen three close friends suffer because they allowed outside forces to determine their behavior.

One friend was hit by his parents as a child and grew up angry. In school he fought classmates, which only made his parents more violent. Later, after he married, he repeated the same pattern with his wife. His rage never faded, and tragically he ended up killing her and himself. By letting those early experiences define him, he destroyed everything.

Another friend fell for girls who played with his emotions. Hurt by their rejection, he stopped caring about their feelings and treated them badly in return. He lost all chance at real love. Even when he finally met someone genuine, he used the same cruel games and ended up completely alone.

My third friend changed himself constantly to satisfy others’ expectations. He acted in ways that pleased the people he cared about but never felt true happiness because he was living a lie.

These examples show that if we let bad experiences or opinions mold our character, we risk becoming someone we will later regret. We must take responsibility for who we are and choose our own path.

For example, I know a person from my country. When we were in class, the teacher said to search on the internet for the story of this person. In math class, we used our phones as calculators. But there was one girl who never did what the teacher said. She started to see Facebook and send messages to her friend in the same class, and that affected the person who received her messages. Sometimes there are students who absolutely do what the teacher or the school says. In that case, it is really a good idea to use the cell phone because it helps us in class or gives us more information about something we want to know.

For example, in my case, I am a person who doesn’t have too much time in this country. Sometimes when I am reading in my English class and find a word or sentence I don’t know, I need to search information to understand what I am doing. It is the same in my math class. Too many times I don’t know how to translate symbols and need to use my phone for that. I think that way is very good. If the school permits us to use our cell phones, it can be the best way to learn more things and make our work in a way that the students like. It can also be more helpful for the students and for the teachers.

I think it all depends on the student. Using cell phones in class can be harmful, or it can also be a good idea for learning in school. The school gives us the opportunity to use our phones, and we should feel grateful for that opportunity. We should use the phone for our work, not for other things that can cause our grades to go down.

Students use cell phones in the classroom for educational purposes.

Teachers sometimes allow us to use our phones during lessons to look up information or complete assignments. This policy can save time and help us concentrate on our work because we can access resources without leaving the classroom. However, some students ignore these instructions and spend their time playing games, browsing social media, or doing other distracting activities instead of paying attention to the lesson.

For instance, when I was studying in my home country, our teacher asked us to research the life story of a famous person online. In math class, we used our phones as calculators. Most of the class followed these directions, but one student opened Facebook and started sending messages to friends. Her behaviour not only distracted her but also disturbed classmates who were trying to focus on their tasks.

On the other hand, many students use their phones in helpful ways. In my experience, I often lack free time, especially since I am learning English in a new country. When I come across words or phrases I don’t understand, I quickly search for their meanings on my phone. The same happens in math lessons when I need to check a formula or translate symbols. Using my phone in this way makes my studies more efficient and helps me learn faster.

In my opinion, whether phones become tools for learning or sources of distraction depends on each student’s responsibility. Since schools now allow us to use our phones, we should appreciate this opportunity and use our devices only for the tasks assigned by teachers. By doing so, we can improve our grades and take full advantage of the educational resources available to us.

First impressions are almost impossible to change. While some people believe they can adjust how others perceive them after an initial meeting, I am convinced that the very first reaction stays with us forever.

For example, when a friend surprises me, my immediate response is to smile. In that instant, I feel so happy and excited that I don’t even notice what’s happening around me. My first words might be “Oh my God, this is amazing!” because I never expected someone in my life to do something so thoughtful. That genuine reaction shows how fixed our first impression can be.

Another proof is how I feel inside during that moment. My tone of voice, my facial expression and even my body language reveal my true emotions. People around me pick up on that excitement and remember it. Nobody can erase or rewrite that initial joy, since it reflects my own choices and feelings at that exact moment.

On a bad day, a surprise from someone special—whether family, friends or a partner—can instantly lift my spirits. In the blink of an eye, sadness turns into happiness. I stopped thinking about my problems and focused only on that bright moment. That pure reaction stays with me long after the surprise ends.

In conclusion, a meaningful surprise creates an unforgettable first impression. Because it comes from the heart and captures genuine emotions, that initial reaction cannot be altered. No matter what happens later, the first impression remains a permanent part of our memory.

Small acts of kindness can profoundly lift someone’s mood. When a person is feeling down, a genuine compliment or a warm smile can brighten their day. Telling someone “I believe in you” or “everything will work out” offers comfort and boosts their confidence. In contrast, harsh or negative comments can deepen their sadness and make them feel worthless. Everyone has a purpose in life; making someone feel insignificant may cause them to lose hope entirely or even consider harming themselves.

People generally fall into two categories: those who offer kindness and those who spread negativity. The choice is ours alone. Nobody can force us to be cruel—it is a decision we make. If caring individuals disappeared, the world would be overwhelmed by hostility and unhappiness. Hurting others only reflects badly on our own character and fills us with bitterness. Instead, we can listen, offer support, or encourage someone to seek help. While it is up to each person to accept assistance, we should all strive to treat others with compassion and respect.

Treating others as we wish to be treated—sometimes called the Golden Rule—is essential. Checking on a friend with a simple “How are you?” shows you care. Staying by someone’s side through both joyful and difficult times strengthens bonds and builds trust. Even small gestures, such as sharing a hopeful message or lending a listening ear, remind people they are not alone. In the end, compassionate words and actions, no matter how small, have the power to change someone’s day—and perhaps even their life. By choosing empathy and respect, we help create a more supportive world for everyone.

I believe that setting a curfew for teenagers can be very helpful because it lowers the risk of accidents and lessens their feelings of isolation. When young people stay off the streets late at night, they are far less likely to break laws or get caught up in violence, crime, or weapon-related incidents. A curfew offers them a measure of protection, at least for a while or until longer-term solutions are found. The government also has a duty to help homeless teens who might otherwise be left to fend for themselves. Dropping out of high school too soon is unfortunate because it shows a lack of willingness to study and develop essential skills. Without a diploma, these youths often face a harsh reality where employers are reluctant to hire them. Once a curfew is in place, many might secure entry-level positions that pay better than anything they could find on the streets, giving them a sense of achievement. Too often, teens make poor choices such as ignoring rules, skipping classes, getting low grades, showing disrespect, or spending excessive time on their phones. If they fail to adjust their behavior, they could end up in serious trouble. Still, I am optimistic that with proper support and guidance, these young people can turn their lives around.

In my science class, we often watch simple experiments that demonstrate chemical changes, such as a flame that shifts color when different substances are added. Seeing bright reds and greens dance in the fire makes science feel alive and exciting. Our teacher clearly enjoys these demonstrations, and that enthusiasm helps us understand how chemicals on Earth can transform in surprising ways. It’s this sense of wonder that shows me science is not just a subject but a joyful exploration of our world.

Becoming a scientist takes dedication and years of study. No one simply wakes up one day and declares, “I am a scientist!” Instead, aspiring researchers attend school and later go to college or university, where they learn to carry out tests and observations methodically. Science covers many fields. For example, science fiction stories often imagine drastic environmental shifts, space travel, or groundbreaking discoveries that push the boundaries of what we know. While these tales are fictional, they inspire real scientists to explore and experiment, sometimes even designing curved swords or building model reactors just for fun.

One useful tool all scientists learn is scientific notation. This method writes large or small numbers as a decimal between one and ten multiplied by a power of ten. For instance, 10 to the third power represents 1,000. Using scientific notation makes complex calculations more manageable, especially when measuring distances in space or counting tiny particles in a lab sample.

There are also specific terms every scientist might encounter. A scintilla, for instance, refers to a person with expert knowledge in one or more scientific areas—someone whose insights shine brightly, much like a spark. In nuclear physics, a chain reaction describes a process where splitting one atom releases neutrons that then split other atoms, sustaining a series of reactions. This principle is the basis for both powerful energy sources and, if uncontrolled, destructive forces. Discovering that atoms can divide and release energy was one of science’s greatest achievements.

Many people who study science truly love their work. Their experiments aren’t just tasks; they’re puzzles to solve and chances to make new discoveries. I dream of becoming a teacher who shares that passion. To anyone else who wishes to follow a scientific path, my advice is simple: embrace your curiosity, attend classes diligently, and never be discouraged by mistakes. My own sister once dated someone who wanted to become a scientist. He dedicated himself entirely to his studies, and eventually they went their separate ways. Although it was painful at first, she later admitted she respected his commitment. She learned that following your ambitions can sometimes mean making tough choices.

No matter what field you aim for, whether nursing, teaching, or research, persistence is essential. In life, no one else can do your assignments or push you forward—you must motivate yourself. Science demands hard work, but it also rewards those efforts with moments of true discovery. If your heart is set on exploring the mysteries of nature, don’t let anyone stop you.

Science is important because it helps us understand everything from the solar system to the tiniest particles. As scientists, we solve problems not only by conducting experiments but also by talking through ideas with teammates and friends. Sharing questions and solutions keeps us from feeling overwhelmed. So find people who support your interests, discuss your challenges, and grow together.

In the end, science belongs to everyone who dares to dream. Whether your dream is to study chemical reactions or map distant stars, trust yourself and keep moving forward. Let nothing—and no one—prevent you from following your passion.

Even if someone insists they do not need help, they may actually need it the most. Mental health can change suddenly, and it can be challenging to support someone who feels upset or confused. Psychologists have a tough job because they work with many people facing different issues, which can be exhausting. Still, their role is crucial for those who require professional support.

I disagree with the proposal to change school policy so that students must maintain at least a B average to participate in sports or other activities. While academics are important, expecting every student to earn a B in all classes is unrealistic. Many students work hard to achieve a C average and deserve the chance to join extracurriculars. A C+ or C average is more attainable than a B because classes vary in difficulty, and this requirement would allow more students to stay engaged.

Requiring a B in every subject might discourage students from taking part in clubs or teams, reducing their motivation. Instead, setting the minimum grade at a C would still encourage academic responsibility without excluding those who struggle. Students with C, B, or A grades should be allowed to participate, as they are passing and showing effort. However, those receiving D or F grades are clearly in danger of failing and should focus on improving their studies before joining sports and activities.

In my view, a policy that bars only students with failing marks from extracurriculars strikes a fair balance. It motivates students to maintain at least a passing grade while giving them the opportunity to benefit from sports and clubs. Raising the bar to a B average is too strict and could harm students’ overall school experience.

I believe that true success comes from facing repeated setbacks without losing enthusiasm. In my opinion, this attitude allows us to turn failures into steps toward achievement.
