I felt isolated and found it hard to start conversations or make friends. Despite these obstacles, I kept practicing my language skills every day. Now, a year later, my English has improved significantly, and I feel much more confident in class and with my peers.

Failure has not only made me stronger, but also led me closer to success. Last year, I even thought about returning to Thailand, but I reminded myself, “Don’t give up—you can try again.” By believing in myself, I stayed, continued to learn, and gained many lessons. Mistakes teach us valuable lessons, and each time we recover from a failure, we grow. If we quit after one setback, we lose the chance to succeed.

Many high school students are tempted by accelerated programs that let them finish in three years instead of the usual four. Yet these schedules often require taking classes after school or during summer, while restricting elective options. Consequently, students spend less time on homework, family, friends, and summer breaks, and miss out on vital electives like foreign languages, nutrition, music, computer skills, or physical education. In some cases, they even cover two levels of the same subject, such as freshman and sophomore English, within one school year. Although early graduation can allow students to start college or enter the workforce sooner, the intense pace raises the risk of burnout or failure—an issue uncommon in traditional programs. For these reasons, most students would benefit from the balanced, four-year high school experience.

I disagree with the idea that students must choose a career path as soon as they enter high school. Forcing young people to decide on a profession so early can create unnecessary stress and limit their chance to explore a variety of subjects.

In some communities, course schedules are tailored to guide students toward a specific occupation before they even know their true strengths or interests. However, most adults only discover their ideal profession after completing their education and gaining practical experience. This process of trial and error helps people make more informed choices as they mature.

To succeed in any field, students should first finish high school, pursue higher education if needed, and then gradually build their skills through work or internships. Expecting them to commit to a career prematurely may prevent them from fully preparing and finding the right match for their talents and ambitions.

Thank you for considering my perspective. If you have any questions, please feel free to contact me.

I believe technology brings many advantages. You can shop online without leaving your house, read books on the internet, and play games with people from anywhere, making new friends all from home.  

Some people are unable to drive to visit friends or family, so they rely on technology to stay in touch. They might call relatives on the other side of the world, chat with new acquaintances, or join online gaming communities. This keeps them connected even if they cannot travel.  

Students also benefit from technology. They use it to research new topics, join school clubs, and complete homework more quickly. Social media platforms like Facebook and Snapchat help them share ideas and stay informed about what their classmates are doing. When guided by schools, technology can be a safe and effective tool for learning.  

Critics say that technology prevents face-to-face interaction and real-world fun. While it is true that spending too much time online can limit in-person experiences, for some people—especially those who work from home or prefer quiet environments—technology provides important social and professional opportunities.  

Older adults can use technology to read millions of books online, from history and sports to science fiction. They can also make video calls to family members, overcoming distance and mobility barriers. Ordering groceries or meals through apps makes life easier for those who cannot go out often.  

Beyond social and leisure uses, many people manage their taxes, pay bills, or even hire specialists through web services. For those who feel anxious about face-to-face conversations, online communities offer a way to connect with like-minded people and share interests.  

Gaming is another area where technology shines. Players can download or stream games, compete in tournaments, and even earn money through streaming platforms or e-sports events.  

In short, technology can improve virtually every aspect of our lives. It makes tasks faster, learning more accessible, and social interaction possible from a distance. By using these tools wisely, we can enjoy safer, more efficient, and more connected lives.

The school board has introduced a plan for all schools to plant more trees and greenery to protect our planet. I fully support this idea because it brings many advantages for people, animals, and the environment.

Every school should hire a gardener or a teacher with gardening experience to guide students. I believe that not every student should take classes online from home. Virtual learning can be convenient, but it also creates challenges for many learners. Below, I will explain three reasons why online coursework at home is not suitable for all students, and then suggest how schools and colleges might use this option more effectively.

First, completing lessons at home can be difficult because learners lose immediate access to their teachers. In a classroom, you can raise your hand and get help right away when you’re stuck. At home, you often have to wait for an email reply or navigate confusing instructions on your own. As a result, students may misunderstand key concepts, feel frustrated, and fall behind. For these reasons, attending classes in person remains the best choice for most learners who need regular guidance.

Second, only the most self-motivated or high-achieving students should be allowed to finish their coursework online. Those who already meet testing standards or maintain a strong grade point average can handle the freedom and responsibility that come with working from home. They know how to organize their time, meet deadlines, and study independently. Granting them this option could free up their schedule and let them focus on advanced projects or part-time jobs. However, struggling students still require the structure and support of traditional school.

Third, online classes should be reserved primarily for younger children in elementary or middle school under special circumstances. Some parents prefer their kids to learn at home for health or travel reasons, and teachers can design simplified assignments that suit a child’s pace. In such cases, having classes online can save families time and reduce stress. Yet for most elementary and middle school students, face-to-face interaction with peers and educators remains crucial for social and academic development.

In conclusion, schools should offer online classes as an option rather than a default. High school students who prove they can work independently might benefit, while younger students or those who need extra help should stay in the classroom. Middle schools could trial limited online programs, and teachers can monitor progress closely to ensure no one falls through the cracks.

Finally, colleges should continue expanding online courses because adult learners generally have better study habits and goals. With more flexible schedules, they can complete classes at home, maintain employment, and earn higher grades before moving on to the next subject.

I disagree with Albert Einstein’s claim that imagination is more important than knowledge. In my opinion, having solid knowledge is essential before we can use our creativity effectively. Without understanding the facts or the situation, it is hard to imagine something useful or realistic.

First, when you want to write a story, you need to know about characters, places, or events before you can picture them clearly in your mind. If you only imagine without any background information, your ideas may be too vague or impossible to develop. By learning the details first, you can guide your imagination toward a coherent plot.

Second, in everyday work, knowledge comes before planning. For example, if you start a new job, you must learn the tasks and rules of the company. Once you understand these, you are better prepared to think of improvements or new methods. Imagination alone cannot replace the practical skills you acquire through study or training.

Third, in science class, we examine plants or other specimens using established methods. You must know how to use tools and follow procedures before you explore new hypotheses. If you skip the basic knowledge, your observations may be incorrect or meaningless.

Finally, even in criminal investigations, the police gather evidence and learn the scene before they imagine how the crime happened. Knowledge of the facts helps them create an accurate reconstruction.

Some people argue that imagination comes first, but I believe knowledge lays the groundwork. With a solid understanding, our creative ideas become more realistic and effective.

I believe the author of the phrase “you will never grow” makes a powerful observation about personal development. I agree that many people fail to appreciate what they already have. In reality, greed, arrogance, and impatience often block genuine progress.

First, greed can damage those who wish to advance in their careers, studies, or personal lives. For example, my brother left school because he thought earning money quickly was more valuable. He now regrets that choice and admits giving up his education was a mistake.

Second, pride leads some individuals to feel superior to others. This attitude can cause them to ignore or even bully their peers. I disagree with this way of thinking, since real achievement comes through hard work and humility, not by putting others down.

Finally, wanting everything at once prevents us from understanding life’s true lessons. Growth does not come from accumulating possessions; it comes from valuing small beginnings and seeking wisdom. A solid education and strong principles help us become better people.

In conclusion, life presents many opportunities, but we must choose carefully. By overcoming greed, pride, and impatience, we can grow into wiser and kinder individuals.

When Thomas Jefferson encouraged us to stay active and engaged, he meant that students need a wide range of experiences to spark their curiosity. By providing various clubs, workshops, and projects, schools can help pupils discover new interests, exchange knowledge with their peers, and bring creative solutions to different challenges. If these opportunities are lacking, students may become bored and struggle to think in innovative ways.

Introducing fun sports or leisure activities also offers a healthy outlet for stress. While continuous studying or practicing can help young people grow and develop important skills, they also deserve time to relax, play, and enjoy their childhood. These breaks from routine can boost their energy and overall well-being, making them more effective when they return to their tasks.

Without such activities, students might spend all their time on work and ignore their family and friends. An overloaded schedule can make it hard to share special moments at home, leading to a sense of isolation and missed memories.

Jefferson also believed in the power of passion. When you follow a dream—whether it’s mastering a sport or pursuing a creative hobby—you gain momentum the more you dedicate yourself. Consistent effort and responsibility teach discipline, and as you see progress, your confidence grows. Finding a goal that brings happiness can guide you through challenges and keep you motivated.

In his writing, Thomas Jefferson aimed to inspire us to be creative, enthusiastic, and resilient. He urged us to seize each moment, try new things, and maintain determination even when problems arise. I share his view, and I think his life is a powerful example of perseverance. By embracing Jefferson’s advice, we can work hard, cherish our experiences, and never give up on our ambitions.

A person’s life can be compared to a brief story in which experiences shape the way they think and act. Some people move smoothly through life, while others face tougher challenges. Whenever someone overcomes a difficulty, they learn lessons that can help them make decisions later on. If another person has gone through a similar experience, their example may inspire positive changes or give hope. After encountering various situations, it is easier to feel motivated by someone else’s journey.

There are many ways to influence someone, and not everyone finds inspiration in the same way. Some people are motivated by hearing about another’s actions, while others prefer to work through problems alone. Inspiration often brings confidence when someone is unsure how to proceed. In that sense, another person’s influence can always be beneficial.

However, an example is not the only way to inspire change. Sometimes you need to look inward and assess your own situation. By thinking carefully about what is best for you, you may discover the right path without turning to others for guidance.

We are all human and prone to making mistakes, and learning from those mistakes is essential. Although different methods of inspiration exist, there are times when you won’t think of anyone else but yourself as a guide. Personal reflection can be just as powerful as seeing someone else succeed.

When people look for inspiration or motivation, they might not realize that they have already faced similar challenges. Yet, everyone is unique, and what worked for one person might not work for another. Instead of trying to copy someone’s life exactly, it is better to view their experience as a model and adapt the positive aspects to your own situation.

Sometimes it’s pure coincidence that two people have the same experience, and they may simply feel understood rather than inspired. Observing how someone else handled a problem can show alternative approaches: What did they do differently? What might you change if the same issue happens again?

It can be comforting to know you are not the only one who has experienced a certain hardship. In those moments, someone else’s story can touch you and encourage you to keep going. Even if the support comes only from within your own mind, thinking of an example can boost your confidence and help you believe that you can succeed too.

Life will always include both good and bad moments, and sometimes you become the person who inspires others. Actions and behaviours can influence those around us, yet each person thinks and reacts in their own way. Still, by sharing our experiences, we offer others a chance to find hope, learn from our journey, and perhaps be inspired to overcome their own challenges.

Technology has become the thread that weaves people from all corners of the globe into one interconnected community. It offers a means of communication that operates in cyberspace, saving time and making it remarkably simple to reach someone miles away in just seconds. Whether through instant messaging, social media, or email, modern tools help people stay in touch without delay. Beyond practical uses, technology also brings enjoyment, as seen in video games, which stand out as one of its most popular innovations.

One of the greatest advantages is that technology removes barriers to connection. It enables friendships and professional relationships to flourish on platforms designed for quick and affordable interaction. No longer do we need to rely on expensive long-distance calls or postal services; a video call or a text message costs little and arrives instantly. This ease of contact makes it possible for families, colleagues, and old friends to maintain relationships smoothly, regardless of geographical distance.

Initially, people struggled with limited ways to reach one another, but technology provided the answer to these constraints. Many researchers have studied how digital tools influence social bonds and have shown that, when used correctly, they encourage people to stay linked. The main goal of technological advancements has always been to improve human life, and communication holds a key place in that mission. By designing systems that let us converse across continents, technology fulfills its promise to make our everyday experiences more convenient and connected.

Smartphones, in particular, have revolutionized how we interact. Today, instead of traveling to visit relatives, we can simply dial their number or open a chat app. News also spreads faster than ever; people worldwide learn about important events as they happen, thanks to online news services and social networks. This rapid flow of information keeps us informed and aware of global developments.

Besides saving time, modern communication costs far less than traditional methods. It offers a low-priced way for anyone wanting to reach out to friends or conduct business. And while technology provides practical benefits, it also caters to entertainment needs. Video games, available in various genres and difficulty levels, engage all age groups and demonstrate how innovation can be both useful and fun.

However, not everyone embraces these advances. A minority of people misunderstand technology because they lack experience or the skills to use it effectively. They may not have learned basic abilities such as typing, reading digital instructions, or navigating online platforms. This knowledge gap makes it hard for them to enjoy technology’s full benefits. Therefore, education plays a vital role: teaching digital literacy ensures that more individuals can write messages, understand online content, and listen to audio or video calls. In this way, learning and technology support each other, making life easier and keeping everyone better connected.

Advice from others helps us learn how to make better choices and avoid problems. When we listen to different people, we can improve our behavior, reach higher goals, and stay safe. Parents, teachers, friends, coaches, and even everyday helpers all offer useful tips that guide us in various parts of life.

First of all, parents play a key role by sharing their experience. If you work alongside your father, for example, he might show you how to handle tasks carefully and teach you the right way to solve problems. By following their suggestions, you gain skills and avoid mistakes. Learning good habits at home lays the groundwork for being a responsible student and family member.

At school, teachers give advice to help you succeed academically. A gym teacher might remind you to follow instructions during exercises so you won’t get hurt and can earn a good grade. In math class, classmates sometimes explain different methods for solving problems, while the teacher points out what to review before a test. Paying attention to these tips makes studying more effective and reduces stress when exams arrive.

Friends also offer support, both in and out of school. A close friend may encourage you to join positive activities or suggest ways to handle peer pressure. Their guidance can help you stay motivated, feel happier, and grow as a person. Similarly, coaches provide practical advice on sports techniques, teamwork, and winning strategies. Teams improve greatly when players apply their coach’s recommendations during practice and games.

Beyond family and school, we often seek advice in daily situations. When shopping, it’s wise to ask someone familiar with the product to know if it is reliable or healthy. Without such guidance, we might make poor choices that affect our well-being. Even a bus driver gives instructions on safe behavior inside the vehicle; following these rules prevents accidents and keeps everyone secure.

In all these ways, listening to advice from many sources helps us learn the right actions, succeed in our tasks, and stay out of trouble. By valuing the guidance we receive, we build knowledge, confidence, and a safer, happier life.

No one knows everything on their own. For example, I learned how to order books over the Internet, but I did not know the best way to shop online. My sister showed me the steps for shopping, and in return I explained my method for ordering books. By exchanging advice, we both gained useful knowledge. This kind of sharing helps everyone become more skilled at different tasks.

Technology also connects us beyond simple shopping. We can play games with friends around the world or stay in touch on social media sites like Facebook, Twitter, and WhatsApp. If we limited ourselves to face-to-face meetings only, life would feel dull for many people. Some enjoy chatting at any hour, and imposing strict limits on online conversations could leave them feeling isolated.

At the same time, it is healthy not to speak to others nonstop. We should maintain connections with the world around us. For instance, thanks to technology we can learn about fires, earthquakes, and other emergencies as soon as they happen. It also helps us communicate with different kinds of people—both those we admire and those we might consider difficult. Even challenging contacts can teach us new information or habits.

If we blindly follow bad advice, we could run into legal trouble or other serious problems. That is why we must be careful about whom we trust. We should keep asking questions and forming our own judgments. If someone proves unreliable, we can stop relying on their advice.

In the end, nobody is perfect, and we all benefit from learning from each other. By combining the freedom of technology with a healthy dose of caution, we can enjoy a richer, more informed life.

Each school studies more than one hundred students. Many high school students do not take many hard subjects; most of them take art and music. Educational programs already require students to take courses during the summer if they do not finish important subjects. Making a rule that students who want to finish high school faster must take courses during the summers or in the evenings—or may not be able to take elective courses—is not a good idea.

Most things in our life need time: hobbies, learning, traveling, and studying in school. Every activity requires time and study too.

What about those who need extra time? What about immigrants, who need extra time for their homework? Will they study well? And do they need this program? They need time to finish their homework. Most of them don’t have time to study well under a four-year education program.

Also, what about teachers? Will this subject be interesting for students to study? Will they have time to explain to students what they study? Teachers need some time to prepare the topics they give to students. They also need time to explain these topics during the lesson and afterward if students don’t understand them in class.

Nobody has extra time.

Of course, some schools can make a three-year education program, but only some schools. Educational programs must have extra time and be interesting to all students.

In many high schools with over a hundred students, a lot of pupils choose easier subjects like art and music. Forcing those who fall behind in core classes to take summer or evening lessons so they graduate faster—and perhaps lose elective options—is not a good idea.

Everyone needs time for hobbies, travel, and regular study. Some learners, especially newcomers from other countries, require extra hours to finish their homework. Packing all of their work into a shorter, four-year program can make it hard for them to learn well.

Teachers would struggle too. They need time to prepare lessons, explain topics clearly in class, and give extra help afterward to anyone who still has questions. A tighter schedule would leave less room for this support.

Only a small number of schools offer a three-year system, and it suits just a few students. Educational programs should allow enough time for both learning and personal interests, and they must be engaging so every student can succeed without feeling overwhelmed.

Do we really achieve more by filling every moment with activity, or can pausing also bring advantages? I believe that students who maintain an active lifestyle throughout their school years—and beyond—tend to develop stronger skills and become experts through constant practice. On the other hand, some argue that taking time to rest prevents exhaustion and keeps us feeling fresh for longer.

Supporters of continuous engagement point out that practice builds expertise. When students repeatedly work on a task a teacher assigns, they gain speed and confidence each time they try. Employers look for this kind of dedication, and having a record of consistent effort—whether in class projects or community service—can earn positive recommendations later on.

Another clear benefit is exercise. Young people who join sports teams improve their endurance and overall health. Learning to train regularly prepares them to handle demanding work in the future, and school sports often offer credits or awards for success. These experiences also introduce students to like-minded peers, creating friendships that stretch beyond the playing field and even across different regions.

Yet it’s important to remember that rest plays a vital role in maintaining our activity level. A good night’s sleep refreshes the mind and body, so students can wake up early and give their best at school. Along with rest, a healthy breakfast fuels us for the day ahead. Without adequate sleep and nutrition, even the most energetic person can struggle to concentrate or participate fully.

Some people believe that taking breaks makes them more productive. Students who choose not to join extracurricular activities often find more time for focused study, which can boost their test scores. Brief moments of downtime also prevent boredom and keep motivation high, so when they return to work, they feel less overwhelmed.

Still, keeping busy offers many rewards that can shape our future. Active participation in class discussions, school plays, clubs, or sports teams helps students set and reach goals. By the end of the school year, they often look back with pride at what they have accomplished. Moreover, colleges and scholarship boards notice applicants who made the most of their high school years through diverse activities and leadership roles.

In the long run, those who stay engaged don’t just benefit themselves—they inspire others too. Their willingness to try new things shows they are not complacent but eager to grow. Financially, this can pay off: a strong work ethic and a broad range of experiences may lead to better job opportunities and higher earnings later in life.

Of course, being active should never feel like a burden. Each student must find the right balance that fits their own energy and interests. But overall, making the most of school life—whether through studying hard, taking part in sports, or joining community projects—seems to offer more advantages than staying idle. By choosing to stay active, students prepare themselves not only for academic success but for a healthier, more fulfilled future.

First impressions have a powerful and lasting impact on our lives, and I firmly believe they are almost impossible to change. From the moment we meet someone or experience something new, our minds form quick judgments that stay with us for years. In this essay, I will explain why first impressions matter so much and offer examples that show how they shape our memories and feelings.

When we encounter someone for the first time, we notice their appearance, voice, and behaviour within seconds. These initial observations create an image in our minds that is difficult to alter later. If a person seems friendly and confident at first, we tend to remember them positively even if they make mistakes afterwards. On the other hand, a negative first encounter can be hard to overcome, no matter how much effort the person puts in later. This shows how strong our early perceptions can be.

One clear example of the power of first impressions comes from childhood. I remember when I was six years old and my parents surprised me with a Spiderman toy. The excitement I felt that day was unforgettable. Holding that toy for the first time made me believe in superheroes and sparked my imagination. Even now, I think back to that moment as if it happened yesterday. This simple gift left an impression on my heart that I cannot erase.

Another illustration is my first visit to the beach. The sound of the waves, the feeling of sand between my toes, and the endless blue water amazed me. That initial encounter with the ocean was so impressive that every time I return to the seaside, I recall my first day there with the same joy and wonder. It shows how a single experience can shape our emotions and expectations for the future.

Finally, many people remember their first day at school, whether it went well or not. Even if they felt nervous or shy, that day usually stands out in their memory because it marked a major step in their lives. No matter how many new faces and classrooms they meet later, the first day remains special and memorable.

In conclusion, first impressions are deeply rooted in our minds and are very hard to change. They influence how we see people and places, and they stay with us as powerful memories. By understanding their importance, we can try to make positive impressions ourselves and appreciate the ones we have experienced. Good impressions at the start can open doors and create lasting happiness.

I do not agree with Winston Churchill’s idea that success comes from moving from one failure to the next without losing enthusiasm. Although his words sound inspiring, they leave out important factors that make success possible. First, simply repeating the same action with enthusiasm does not guarantee improvement. If a person fails many times at the same method, they may end up stuck and never achieve their goal. Instead, it is better to look for different approaches or solutions rather than expect a better result by doing exactly the same thing again.

Second, failure itself has an important role in our lives, but it can also mark a clear end if we do not change our strategy. Every person decides how to react after failing. If someone gives up once they hit an obstacle, they will never discover any positive outcome. By examining what went wrong and seeking new answers, they might turn a failure into a stepping stone for future success.

For example, my personal goal is to finish college and earn a degree. I stay motivated and optimistic, but I also know that studying more effectively or asking for help are practical ways to overcome difficulties. If one exam does not go well, I plan a different study schedule or ask a tutor for guidance. This shows that enthusiasm alone is not enough; we need to adapt and look for solutions.

In life, we face many situations where a straightforward solution does not seem possible. Yet by exploring different paths and remaining hopeful, we often find at least one way forward. Ultimately, success is not just about never losing energy; it is about combining that energy with careful problem solving. That is why I disagree with Churchill’s statement: perseverance without searching for better methods can lead to repeated failure rather than true success.

A city council is considering a 10 p.m. curfew on weekdays and a midnight limit on weekends for teenagers. Supporters argue that such rules protect young people from harm, while critics say they intrude on teens’ freedom. In my view, curfews help keep teenagers safe and encourage responsibility without causing unfair interference.

First, late hours can be unsafe for adolescents. Walking around streets at night exposes them to risks like accidents, crime, or simply being in the wrong place at the wrong time. If police stop a teenager who is out past curfew, officers often have to call parents to pick them up. This not only creates stress for families but also reinforces that teens underage shouldn’t be alone after dark.

Parents also worry when their children miss the agreed-upon return time. Young people might think night outings are exciting, but friends won’t always protect them from danger. A curfew reminds teens that their wellbeing comes first and that trusting adults set rules with good reasons. Darkness makes it harder to spot hazards, especially if drivers are impaired or streets are deserted.

Moreover, curfews are legal requirements, and breaking them can lead to serious consequences. Law enforcement takes these rules seriously because they aim to reduce juvenile crime and keep neighborhoods secure. Teens who obey the curfew show respect for their parents and the community, preserving trust rather than damaging relationships over a late-night adventure.

Finally, curfews give young people choices: stay home and relax, finish homework, watch a movie, or plan daytime activities with friends. Rather than sneaking out to grab a snack or meet a partner, teens can use evenings safely at home. This also teaches them to balance social life with family expectations.

In conclusion, a reasonable curfew protects teenagers from potential dangers, strengthens parent-child trust, and promotes respect for rules. By going home on time, young people avoid unnecessary risks and prove they can handle independence responsibly.

The city council has recently approved a 10 p.m. curfew for teenagers, and I agree that this rule is necessary. First, a curfew helps young people get enough rest. When teens stay out very late, especially on weekends, they often feel tired in class. Research shows that students with set bedtimes concentrate better and earn higher grades than those who stay out without restrictions.

Second, keeping teenagers off the streets after dark can reduce crime and risky behavior. Late at night, teens are more likely to encounter dangerous situations, whether it’s vandalism, fights, or gang activity. If a young person is found outside past 10 p.m., the police can intervene immediately, guiding them home rather than waiting for a more serious problem to arise.

Some community members worry that the rule interferes with teenagers’ freedom. They argue that curfews treat all young people as if they might cause trouble. However, this law is not meant to punish responsible teenagers but to protect everyone’s safety. It gives parents peace of mind, knowing the police will check on any child roaming the streets late at night.

A curfew can also prevent heartbreaking news calls to parents. Instead of notifying a mother that her child was injured or worse, officers simply ensure teens return safely. Over time, young people will understand the importance of rules and learn to plan their evenings responsibly.

In conclusion, a 10 p.m. curfew for teenagers is not an unnecessary restriction but a practical measure to support better sleep habits, lower crime rates, and protect youth from harm. It encourages cooperation between families, police, and the community, making the city a safer place for everyone.
